measure: persistence_years = years a recognized, normatively significant inadequacy of the governing standard remained uncorrected (from the earliest dated recognition to the correction, or to supersession of the regime)

pairs.matched_on: same domain and overlapping era (1999-2011); the same evidence source (browser implementers and web authors reporting the same limitations of HTML 4.01 / XHTML); resources run AGAINST the hypothesis (the better-resourced, more formal body is the fixed arm)

revising_arm.mechanism: standing living-standard process; continuous editor-driven revision from GitHub issues; founded 2004 after a W3C workshop by Apple/Mozilla/Opera over the W3C's lack of interest in evolving HTML
revising_arm.note: recognized inadequacy (HTML could not express rich web applications) addressed continuously from founding; Web Forms/Web Apps work folded into HTML5 from ~2004-2006 onward

fixed_arm.mechanism: version-and-freeze; HTML 4.01 frozen Dec 1999; effort redirected to XHTML 1.0/1.1/2.0; conformance checked by the W3C Markup Validator = outcome monitoring against a fixed grammar
fixed_arm.note: same recognized inadequacy left standing until the W3C rechartered an HTML Working Group in 2007 to adopt WHATWG's work; the XHTML2 WG was closed end of 2009

pairs.domain: web markup language (same institution, before vs after)
pairs.matched_on: the organization, its domain and its evidence sources are held constant; only the revision regime varies (within-body natural experiment, the strongest control against the resource/evidence confound)

revising_arm.mechanism: MOU with WHATWG signed 28 May 2019: HTML/DOM developed as a single Living Standard at WHATWG, W3C endorses Review Drafts; defects handled continuously via GitHub issues
revising_arm.note: under the living regime a recognized defect is opened as an issue and addressed in due course (issue-to-fix typically days to months, not years)

fixed_arm.note: HTML held a numbered frozen standard; living/no-version model adopted for HTML at W3C only after 2011 (spec became version-less) and formalized 2019

pairs.matched_on: same domain (character encoding); both regimes received external national-body and user-community demand for missing scripts (comparable evidence independence); resources roughly comparable (ISO is a large body)

revising_arm.mechanism: standing mechanism: versioned releases, a public 'Report Error in Publication/Data' ticket and posted errata, a script/character proposal pipeline, and a Unicode Technical Committee empowered to authorize and execute additions; new scripts absorbed version by version. Stability policy deliberately freezes encoded characters, names and normalization = selective non-revision (matches the routine-work limit, CLAIM-665)
revising_arm.note: e.g. the recognized representational inadequacy of a single default skin tone for human emoji was corrected by skin-tone modifiers in Unicode 8.0 (2015) after public criticism; new scripts added each release

fixed_arm.body: pre-Unicode code-page regime (ASCII + ISO/IEC 8859 parts, national code pages)
fixed_arm.mechanism: each part effectively frozen; the regime's response to new-script demand was to mint new incompatible code pages, not to revise one governing standard; conformance = outcome monitoring against a chosen code page
fixed_arm.note: the multilingual-interchange inadequacy (mojibake; scripts unrepresentable in one document) persisted for roughly two decades and was resolved only by Unicode superseding the regime; many scripts never received an 8859 part. End date taken as ~2007 when UTF-8 passed ASCII in web use; the inadequacy was never corrected WITHIN the regime

unmatched_extreme.why_unmatched: no comparable resourced, evidence-independent REVISING partner in the same era; included only to bound the relationship at the no-revision-organ extreme
unmatched_extreme.body: Julian calendar (no standing organ empowered to revise the civil/ecclesiastical calendar)
unmatched_extreme.mechanism: no standing revision body; correction required an ad hoc papal commission and bull
unmatched_extreme.note: drift from the Council of Nicaea (325) reference equinox recognized by Bede (8th c., ~3 days) and Roger Bacon (c.1200-1267, 7-8 days); corrected only by the bull Inter gravissimas (24 Feb 1582), dropping 10 days (4 Oct -> 15 Oct 1582). Taking recognition from Nicaea itself gives ~1257 years
